speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when you first noticed them?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing any involuntary muscle stiffness, tremors, or a feeling of restlessness that makes it difficult to sit still? Do you notice any abnormal movements in your face, such as grimacing or tongue protrusion, or do the symptoms seem to come and go rather than being constant?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms strongly suggest akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. I will prescribe benztropine to help relieve the restlessness and adjust your current medication regimen. DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced akathisia
